11378.html:
11378 várdhana² 'strengthening', n. 'means of strengthening' RV., 'increasing' MBh. 2. '*sweeping', vardhanī-² f. 'broom' lex. (so called because a swept house prospers BPL § 54, or because mention of the removal of anything is ill-omened Molesworth MD 746). [√vr̥dh]
    1. Pa. vaddhana- n. 'increase', Pk. vaḍḍhaṇa-, vaddhaṇa- n., S. vadhiṇī f., Si. väḍun.
    2. Pa. pathavi-vaḍḍhanaka-kamma- n. 'work of sweeping the earth'; Pk. vaḍḍhaṇī-, °ṇiā- f. 'broom', A. bārni, B. bāṛhan, Or. baṛhaṇi, baṛhiṇā, (Gaṛjād) bāṛhuṇī, (Sambhalpur) bāṛhni (whence banneibā 'to sweep'), Bi. baṛhanī, Mth. bāṛhan, Bhoj. bāṛhanī, H. baṛhnī, M. vāḍhṇī, vāḍhvaṇ f.; — N. baṛārnu 'to sweep', baṛār 'broom' < Ap. vaḍḍhāraï 'causes to increase'. — Connexion, if any, is not clear with Paš. chil. barwṓṛ, kuṛ. bārwṓ 'broom', Shum. bóroṛ, Woṭ. byār f., Gaw. ḍaṇḍ-bār 'large broom with handle', bā́rik 'small broom' Buddruss Woṭ 94.

13393.html:
13393 sicyátē 'is sprinkled' RV. [√sic]
    Pk. siccaṁta- pres. part. 'being sprinkled'; Kho. (Lor.) čičeik 'to pour from one vessel to another' (or < śucyati); A. xisiba 'to sprinkle, scatter, sow broadcast, bale', xisani 'baling scoop'; — with -jj- after act. siñj- < siñcáti: L. sijjaṇ 'to be moistened', awāṇ. sijjuṇ 'to be wet'; P. sijjṇā 'to be watered', caus. sijāuṇā (see also svidyati).
    *siñca- 'emission'. [Replaces sḗka-. — √sic]
    *niḥsiñca-.
    Addenda: sicyátē: Garh. sīcṇu 'to sprinkle' or < sin̄cáti.

9188.html:
9188 bahukāra 'effecting much' VS. [bahukara- Pāṇ., m. 'sweeper' lex. (derisory hon. term? Cf. H. mehtar 'id.': see vardhana-²), bahukarā-, °rī- f. 'broom' lex. — bahú-, kāra-¹]
    Pa. bahukāra- 'of great service'; Pk. baühārī-, bahuriyā-, bōhārī- f. 'brush'; S. ḇuhā̆ru m. 'sweepings, refuse', ḇuhārī f. 'broom'; L. bohār m. 'sweepings, dust', (Ju.) ḇohār m., bohārī f. 'broom'; P. buhārā m., °rī, bahārī, °rū f. 'broom'; H. buhārū m. 'sweeper'. — Deriv.: S. ḇuhāraṇu 'to sweep', P. H. buhārnā, G. bārvũ 'to sweep', borvũ 'to clean (a privy)'.
    Addenda: bahukāra-: S.kcch. bauār m. 'rubbish, dirt', b° kaḍhṇū 'to sweep', bauārī f. 'broom'.

13933.html:
13933 svidyati 'sweats' KātyŚr., °tē Yājñ. [√svid]
    Pa. sijjati 'sweats', Pk. sijjaï; L. sijjaṇ 'to be moistened'; P. sijjṇā 'to be wet, be soaked', kgr. sijjā 'damp' (cf. esp. sijj-pasijj jāṇā < *prasvidyati: but see sicyatē); H. sījnā 'to sweat, exude'. — In Pa. sijjati intr. 'boils', H. sījnā intr. 'to simmer (of pot on low fire)' derivation fr. svidyati is supported by svinná- 'sweating' VS. ~ 'seethed, boiled' Hariv.; but the latter meaning may be a reflection of a MIA. pp. of śrīṇā́ti and the Pa. and H. words be < *śrīyatē.

997.html:
997 *āī 'mother, aunt'. [Prob. a nursery word]
    Dm. yī 'mother', yai 'grandmother'; Paš. āī́ 'mother' (→ Par. āi IIFL iii 3, 1), Kal. ā́yΛ, Bshk. īēī; S. āī f. 'mother, aunt, respectful address for any senior female relative'; N. āi-māi 'wife, woman'; A. āi 'mother, smallpox', āiṭi 'affectionate address for a girl'; B. āī 'mother's mother, mother's aunt'; Or. āī 'mother's mother'; G. āi f. 'mother, grandmother'; M. āī f. 'mother, term of endearment for an infant', āī-bāī f. 'motherly old woman', āī-māī f. 'mother, motherly person'. — The Dard. words poss. < āryikā-.
    Addenda: *āī-: S.kcch. āī f. 'mother'; WPah.kc. ai.
